title: Emergency Access & Audit Snapshot — Secrets Evidence Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines an operational pattern for emergency access to secrets ("break-glass"), the snapshotting of credential evidence, and reliable SIEM export of audit events in RBAC v2 environments. It focuses on minimizing blast radius, preserving tamper-evident evidence, and ensuring auditability for post-incident review and compliance requests.

Scope:
- Applies to all production vaults, credential stores, and short-lived token brokers managed by Redwood Inference.
- Covers emergency issuance, temporary role elevation, automated rotation hooks, evidence capture, and SIEM export mappings.
- Not a replacement for change control or normal rotation flows — only for exceptions where normal processes would cause unacceptable downtime.

High-level decision flow (quick):
1) Identify the outage/need and confirm business justification.
2) Try non-credential mitigations (feature toggle, traffic reroute). If none viable -> proceed.
3) Escalate to on-call security lead + on-call SRE and notify product owner.
4) If approved, issue timeboxed contingency credential with automated evidence snapshot.
5) Perform change and rotate/expire contingency credential within defined TTL.
6) Run post-incident evidence collection and report.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Incident Commander (IC): product/SRE lead running the event.
- Security Approver: member of security-on-call authorized to greenlight break-glass.
- Vault Operator: executes token issuance and rotation automation.
- Evidence Custodian: owner of the evidence storage bucket and WORM policy.
- Auditor: compliance reviewer who validates post-incident artifacts.

RBAC v2 mapping notes (practical):
- Principle of least privilege is enforced by role slices. RBAC v2 roles relevant to secrets ops:
  - secrets-reader: view-only metadata and audit logs.
  - secrets-redeem: limited ability to use credentials but not extract raw secrets (for services).
  - secrets-issue-temp: issues short-lived contingency tokens with explicit justification label.
  - secrets-admin: full management (reserved for small group + break-glass timeboxed escalation).
- Implementation guidance: avoid granting secrets-admin to humans for routine ops. Use secrets-issue-temp tied to an approval webhook that records approver and justification.

Emergency credential issuance (step-by-step):
1) IC files a short incident note in channel #sec-incident with header: [EMERGENCY] <service> <impact> <justification>.
2) Security Approver responds with single-line approval: APPROVE <ticket-id> <TTL-minutes>.
3) Vault Operator calls the secure issuance endpoint (internal API): POST /v1/issue-contingency-token with body {service, ticket_id, approver, justification, ttl_minutes, scope}. The issuance endpoint must:
  - generate credential with max TTL <= 60 minutes (policy default).
  - attach metadata: approver, ticket_id, ic, correlation_id.
  - trigger evidence snapshot job and SIEM event.
4) Evidence snapshot job captures:
  - token fingerprint (sha256 of token value), not raw token when possible.
  - issuing principal, approver, TTL, and pre- and post-state of relevant secret versions.
  - system time, monotonic timestamp, and unique evidence_id (uuid).
  - hash of the snapshot bundle signed with KMS key.
5) Vault Operator performs the change.
6) Immediately rotate or revoke the contingency token and rotate associated credentials via automated rotation pipeline.
7) IC compiles incident wrap-up and hands to Auditor for validation.

Evidence automation (detailed):
- Trigger points: issuance, revocation, rotation_complete, failed_rotation, and manual snapshot request.
- What to capture:
  - Audit event JSON (see schema below).
  - Snapshot manifest (list of secret names, versions, checksums).
  - Signed bundle: manifest + audit JSON + operator note, signed by customer or platform KMS (signing key id recorded).
  - Storage: write bundle to WORM bucket with path: s3://redwood-evidence/<org>/<env>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/evidence_<evidence_id>.tar.gz
  - Retention: follow legal retention matrix; default 7 years for incidents hitting PII or regulated data.
- Integrity: compute sha256 checksum for bundle and store checksum both in the object metadata and in the audit event sent to SIEM.

Audit log schema (minimal required fields):
- event_id: uuid
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- service: "vault" | "token-issuer" | "rotation-service"
- action: e.g., issue_token, revoke_token, rotate_secret, snapshot_created
- principal: canonical identity (user:<email> or svc:<service-id>)
- principal_role: resolved RBAC role(s) at time of action
- target: secret path or token id
- target_version: optional
- result: success | failure
- correlation_id: uuid (ties issuance -> snapshot -> SIEM event)
- evidence_id: uuid (if snapshot created)
- signature_kms_key: key-id used to sign bundle
- bundle_checksum: sha256 hex

Example audit JSON (single-line for SIEM ingest):
{"event_id":"3f8a6b8e-9c0f-4b2a-8b1d-2a9b7f6c0d5e","timestamp":"2025-01-10T18:12:34Z","service":"token-issuer","action":"issue_token","principal":"user:ava.martinez@redwood.com","principal_role":"secrets-issue-temp","target":"contingency-token:svc-payments-prod","result":"success","correlation_id":"c0a80123-0000-4b2a-9b1d-abcdef123456","evidence_id":"evi-20250110-0001","signature_kms_key":"projects/redwood/keys/evidence-sign-v1","bundle_checksum":"a3f1..."}

SIEM export and mapping guidance:
- Export pipeline must be append-only and resilient. Recommended stack: Fluentd -> Kafka -> SIEM (Splunk/Elastic). If using Logstash, implement the following:
  - Tag events with source_type=redwood:secrets
  - Use ingestion-time enrichment to add org_id and env tags from the correlation_id map.
  - Keep raw JSON in a _raw field for forensic rehydration.
- Suggested Logstash filter (pseudocode):
  grok { match => { "message" => "%{JSON:json}" } }
  json { source => "json" target => "_json" }
  mutate { add_tag => [ "redwood_secrets" ] }
- Index mapping: store event_id, timestamp, service, action, principal, principal_role, target, result, correlation_id, evidence_id, and bundle_checksum as explicit fields for fast queries.

Tamper-evidence & chain-of-custody:
- Each evidence bundle must be signed by a KMS key with an auditable key rotation policy. Record signing_key_id and key_version in the audit event.
- WORM storage policy prevents delete for retention window. Additional object immutability metadata must be exported to SIEM.
- When copying bundles to long term archive, keep original checksum and signature metadata.

Rotation automation hooks (ideas & safe patterns):
- All contingency-related artifacts trigger a post-hook: /internal/hooks/on-contingency-rotate which enqueues rotation jobs for all dependent consumers.
- Rotation jobs should be idempotent and report status to the audit pipeline. Use coordinator job with per-consumer backoff.
- For services that cannot do secret reload without restart, the rotation job records pre/post config hashes and schedules a maintenance window via the incident ticket system.

Break-glass TTL, limits and controls:
- Default max TTL for a contingency token: 60 minutes.
- Allow extension only via re-approval by Security Approver with explicit business justification and new evidence snapshot.
- Token issuance rate limiting: 3 contingency tokens per service per 30 days.
- All break-glass issuance requires a post-incident RCA and evidence bundle uploaded to compliance. Failure to submit RCA blocks future issuance for the service until remediated.

Post-incident validation checklist (for Auditor):
- Confirm evidence bundle exists and checksum matches audit event.
- Verify signature against KMS key and that key version was valid at time of signing.
- Validate RBAC role mapping for principal at time of event.
- Check SIEM receipt: search correlation_id across all relevant indices for issuance, snapshot_created, rotation_complete.
- Confirm token has been revoked and no active consumers reference old secret versions.

Testing & exercises:
- Quarterly tabletop: simulate a non-PII emergency to walk through approval and issuance (no real tokens minted).
- Annual live drill: issue contingency token against sandbox and validate evidence automation end-to-end (must be scheduled with product owner).
- Automation tests: unit test the snapshot signing, hash calculation, SIEM export, and S3 write using test KMS keys.

Appendix — helpful commands / endpoints:
- Issue (internal): curl -X POST https://internal.api/v1/issue-contingency-token -H "Authorization: Bearer <op-token>" -d '{"service":"svc-payments-prod","ticket_id":"SEC-3421","approver":"user:noah.chen@redwood.com","justification":"card gateway failover","ttl_minutes":45}'
- Snapshot retriever: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-evidence/<org>/<env>/<date>/evidence_<evidence_id>.tar.gz -
- Verify signature: kms verify --key-id projects/redwood/keys/evidence-sign-v1 --signature-file sig.bin --payload-file manifest.json

Open questions & improvements backlog:
- Can we avoid storing any raw contingency token values in evidence bundles (today we store token fingerprint only)?
- Tighten automation to auto-create follow-up Jira tickets for every break-glass issuance.
- Integrate evidence bundle immutability metadata as first-class fields in the SIEM index for faster legal searches.

Contact list (on-call rotation):
- Security on-call: security-oncall@redwood.com (primary: Priya Kapoor)
- SRE on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.com (primary: Liam O'Neill)
- Vault operator pager: vault-ops@redwood.com (Escalation: Noah Chen)

This playbook is intended to be operational and minimal-friction while preserving a strong audit trail. If you make a local change to the issuance API or evidence format, update the audit log schema above and notify the SIEM team to align ingestion mappings.
